cells.tense: The steady one is here now, pen in hand, keeping the old form level.
cells.act: persist on hope that has been tested
cells.ask: Take the thing you already chose — the weekly meal, the letter, the song — and keep at it, with the doubt still sitting there beside you and nothing settled.
cells.core:
You can keep a thing going through a lean season and stay inside it, not just above it. Money is short, time is short, doing it again wears on you, and you carry those and the practice both. Old forms survive because somebody holds them past the point where they pay off, and that's the work of this stretch.
What this can feed next is the longer haul — not a rescue, a continuation. The thing you started before it got hard is still the thing above you, and the doubt hasn't moved it. Go on with the version you picked, through another stretch of not knowing. What you've kept alive this long is its own evidence, whether or not anyone outside it notices.
cells.sheetLine: You carry the pressure and keep the practice alive.
cells.verb: persisting through material pressure by drawing on what you carry inside
cells.place: in the shared meanings, rituals and languages that carry wisdom forward between people

cells.tense: You are bracing already for the lean year before it has arrived in the room.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Someone offers to take part of your load — a meal, an hour, a hand. Accept it, and don't give anything back that same day.
cells.core:
You hold what needs holding, and lately you hold it clenched. Three seasons into next year's trouble before it arrives, you weigh the practice for its survival value and count the people in it as assets or costs. Strength in excess stops containing and starts gripping — the grip reads as care from outside and feels like a jaw set tight from inside.
Strength that holds rather than crushes comes back through exchange, not through more endurance. Something given and something taken, at the size they actually are. Let one exchange with somebody run both directions: receive what's offered against what you've carried, and treat that as the whole transaction for now. It doesn't have to settle the same afternoon. A practice outlasts a person through exchange, not through grip.

cells.tense: What was carried steady has gone still, and the hand is in its old position.
cells.act: let what you gave up be seen by the people it was for, without a word about it
cells.ask: Do the next piece somewhere the person it's for can watch you do it — the doing itself, not the reason.
cells.core:
The pressure is on you and there's no push left to meet it. You go through the motions of the practice, what you carry stays private, and the door you were standing at is behind you. Not laziness — the endurance ran down. The old forms still get repeated, but the part of you that chose them isn't in the repetition, and people nearby can feel that without naming it.
What's needed isn't more effort forced into the flat spot. Do the next piece where it can be watched, by whoever it's for, and stop there. No speech, no explanation offered. What you set aside becomes visible again when somebody sees it happening, and their watching does what your pushing can't. This was meant to be carried where people are, not kept to yourself.

cells.tense: The keeping is happening right now and the hand has already signed it someone else's.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: Pick the smallest true form of the practice you keep — one verse, one dish, one call — and do it once, alone, with nothing riding on it.
cells.core:
You keep the thing going — a recipe, a language, a yearly gathering nobody else remembers to hold — and if anyone asked, it keeps itself. It doesn't. You call the persistence a family habit, or a thing that has to be done, and the people who watch you do it have a different word for it.
Go back to the first time you chose this, before it became a duty, when you were still following it without proof it would last. Pick the smallest true form of it and do that once, alone, with nothing riding on it. No credit deflected, no story told about why. What you've carried privately turns out to have been yours the whole time, and the form was small enough to hold in one hand.
cells.sheetLine: What keeps the practice alive has your handwriting on it.
cells.verb: persisting through material pressure by drawing on what you carry inside
cells.place: in the shared meanings, rituals and languages that carry wisdom forward between people
